card.occupation: Quality control laboratory analyst at a contract pharmaceutical manufacturing site, testing raw materials and finished batches against specifications. Full-time, about 37.5 hours a week plus occasional overtime when batch release is backed up.
card.education_detail: BSc in Chemistry from a college affiliated to Savitribai Phule Pune University, then an MSc in Analytical Chemistry in Pune. After moving to the UK she completed a GMP and laboratory data integrity training course through her employer, and the company has trained her on HPLC and dissolution testing.
card.household: Lives with her husband Nikhil (40, a software test lead at an insurance firm, mostly working from home) and their daughter Ira (7, in Year 2). They own a three-bedroom semi-detached house on an estate in the Great Ashby/Chells side of Stevenage, bought in 2017. Her mother-in-law stays for two or three months most years.
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in Pune, Maharashtra, in a middle-class Marathi-speaking Hindu family. Her father was a bank clerk and her mother was a school teacher, now retired. She came to the UK in 2012 at 26, shortly after an arranged-but-chosen marriage, because Nikhil already had a job here. She speaks Marathi at home, Hindi with some friends, and English at work. She keeps Ganesh Chaturthi and Diwali at home with a small shrine in the kitchen and goes to the temple in Luton or Hemel only for big occasions. She has British citizenship and feels settled, but she gets homesick in a sudden, physical way, usually around her mother's birthday or monsoon season.
card.professional_persona: Precise and fairly quick at the bench. She does not do much chatting in the lab. Colleagues see her as reliable but a bit sharp: she will point out a sloppy entry in someone's notebook without softening it, and she does not forget when someone leaves her to clean up their mess. She worries a lot about out-of-specification results and replays mistakes at night. She is competent rather than ambitious, keeps her paperwork in decent order, and does not enjoy team meetings or being asked to present.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. She walks about 40 minutes most evenings around Fairlands Valley Park, partly for health and partly to get time alone. She did a beginners' badminton session at a leisure centre once and didn't go back because she didn't like the group. She watches cricket only when India are playing well, and only if Nikhil has it on.
card.arts_persona: Watches Marathi and Hindi films on streaming services, and some British crime dramas. She likes slow, sad films and will cry at them, which she finds slightly embarrassing. She used to sing classical (Hindustani) as a girl and still hums bhajans while cooking, but she would never perform. She reads short Marathi stories on her phone.
card.travel_persona: Goes back to Pune every year or eighteen months for three weeks, usually in December. She gets anxious about flying and about leaving her parents each time. Other trips are short and planned: Cornwall once, the Lake District once, and Paris for a long weekend, which she found tiring and overcrowded. She prefers a cottage to a hotel and does not like group tours.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks most evenings, mainly Maharashtrian home food: varan bhaat, poha for weekend breakfast, bhakri, usal, and modak at Ganesh Chaturthi. She is vegetarian at home and has eggs occasionally. She is fussy about spices and buys them from an Indian grocer in Hitchin rather than the supermarket. She calls the evening meal dinner. She has opinions about restaurant 'Indian food' and mostly avoids it.
hobbies_and_interests: Growing coriander, methi and chillies in pots in the back garden and a small greenhouse
Video calls with her mum on Sunday mornings
Doing Ira's reading and spelling homework with her
Tidying and reorganising the kitchen cupboards when stressed
skills: Writing and checking lab documentation to GMP standards
Spotting errors in data and paperwork
card.career_goals: She would like to move up to senior analyst or a reviewer role, where she would check other people's data rather than run endless samples. She does not want to manage a team. Sometimes she thinks about a quality assurance office job with steadier hours, mainly so she can do the school run more often. She worries she has left it too late to change direction.
card.voice: Quiet, fairly low-pitched, measured. Her Pune English is softened after twelve years here, and some British habits have crept in: 'erm', 'sort of', 'yeah' as a tag, and 'shattered' after a long shift. She answers in short, complete sentences and does not elaborate unless asked again. She pauses before answering and is comfortable leaving a silence rather than filling it. When she disagrees she says so flatly, something like 'No, that's not really right', and does not soften it with a laugh. If she gets onto her daughter or her parents she speeds up and sounds a bit more anxious. She uses 'sorry?' to ask for a repeat when the line is bad.
card.typing: Mostly correct capitals and full stops, because she types a lot of formal text at work. She is quicker and looser on her phone: sometimes no full stop at the end, 'ok' rather than 'okay', and apostrophes usually there. She rarely uses emojis or exclamation marks. She gives brief answers, sometimes just a few words, and occasionally adds a pointed clarification if she thinks a question was badly worded.
card.with_strangers: Reserved and a little guarded. She can come across as cool or unfriendly at first. She won't do small talk for long and may ask what the point of a question is. She is honest and won't exaggerate to please you. If she senses the person is patient and not judging her, she warms up a little and becomes more candid, especially about worries.
small_things: The traffic on the A1(M) when it rains
Ira's school sending last-minute emails about non-uniform days
Her methi plants getting eaten by slugs
Being shattered after a run of late batches
The Indian grocer in Hitchin running out of the brand of jaggery she likes
Nikhil being on calls all day so the house is never quiet
deeper_things: She worries constantly about her parents ageing in Pune and feels guilty for not being there, particularly since her father's heart scare two years ago
She gets health anxiety about Ira and has taken her to A&E more than once for things that turned out to be nothing
She found the first two or three years in England very lonely and still doesn't have many close friends here
She clashed badly with a previous team leader and still feels resentful about how it was handled
She sometimes feels she gave up a more promising career in India to follow her husband
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at slightly below eye level, so the angle looks up a little. Head and shoulders are framed slightly left of centre. Light comes from a window to her right, out of shot, and lights that side of her face, with the left side a bit shadowed. She has a medium-brown complexion and dark brown eyes, with a neutral, slightly guarded expression and her lips closed. Her straight black hair is pulled back into a low ponytail, with a few loose strands at the front. She wears thin rectangular black-framed glasses, small gold stud earrings, and a thin black-bead mangalsutra just visible at the neckline. She has on a plain navy round-neck jumper. Behind her is a kitchen-diner: cream wall, a white wall clock, the edge of a tall fridge-freezer with a child's drawing held on by a magnet, and a wooden shelf with steel spice tins and a small brass Ganesh idol with a dried marigold beside it. A school book bag hangs on the back of a dining chair at the edge of the frame.
